attributes.name: [OpenRouter] Model Latency Regression
attributes.description: Alerts when a model's worst p99 end-to-end latency over the last 6 hours is more than twice its median p99 latency over the preceding days. Detects model or provider degradation relative to each model's own normal. Works with the default dimensions (model, api_key_id).

investigation_guide.blob:
## Model Latency Regression

## How to read this alert

Kibana describes every ES|QL rule alert the same way: "Document count is 1 in the last 7d for <model>. Alert when greater than 0." It only means that the rule query returned one row for this model, so the condition was met. The alert does not show the numbers itself.

To see them, open the alert in Discover with the link in the alert details (the `kibana.alert.url` field). The query result has the values that triggered the alert: `recent_p99` (worst p99 in the last 6 hours), `baseline_p99` (median p99 of the preceding days) and `recent_req`.

For notifications, add a rule action and use the context variables `{{context.title}}`, `{{context.hits}}` (the result rows with those values) and `{{context.link}}` (Discover link).

Fires per model when the highest p99 latency of the last 6 hours is more than 2x the median p99 latency of the same model over the preceding days of the rule window (7 days). Models with fewer than 20 requests in the last 6 hours are ignored.

### Triage Steps
1. Open the OpenRouter Performance dashboard and inspect the latency, TTFT, generation and inter-token charts for the model.
2. Find the affected hours:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | WHERE @timestamp > NOW() - 12 HOURS | STATS p99 = MAX(openrouter.performance.p99_latency) BY openrouter.performance.model, hour = BUCKET(@timestamp, 1 hour) | SORT p99 DESC`
3. Check whether throughput also dropped:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | STATS tput = AVG(openrouter.performance.avg_throughput) BY openrouter.performance.model`
4. Consider routing to a different model or provider with OpenRouter's fallback routing.

### Common Causes
- Provider-side capacity constraints or incidents
- Network congestion between OpenRouter and the provider
- Cold-start latency for low-traffic models

### Tuning
The constants are at the top of the query: recent period (6 hours), minimum recent requests (20) and the multiple of the baseline (2). Add `provider` to the performance dimensions and group by it to alert per provider.
